Cisgender men with [gynecomastia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gynecomastia "Gynecomastia") have not been found to have an increased risk of breast cancer.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-pmid24741509-314) It has been suggested that a 46,XY [karyotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karyotype "Karyotype") (one [X chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_chromosome "X chromosome") and one [Y chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y_chromosome "Y chromosome")) may be protective against breast cancer compared to having a 46,XX karyotype (two X chromosomes).[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-pmid24741509-314) Men with [Klinefelter's syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klinefelter's_syndrome "Klinefelter's syndrome") (47,XXY karyotype), which causes [hypoandrogenism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypoandrogenism "Hypoandrogenism"), [hyperestrogenism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperestrogenism "Hyperestrogenism"), and a very high incidence of gynecomastia (80%), have a dramatically (20- to 58-fold) increased risk of breast cancer compared to karyotypical men (46,XY), closer to the rate of karyotypical women (46,XX).[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-pmid24741509-314)[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-pmid18369226-315)[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-Li2009-316) The incidences of breast cancer in karyotypical men, men with Klinefelter's syndrome, and karyotypical women are approximately 0.1%,[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-PelengarisKhan2013-317) 3%,[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-pmid18369226-315) and 12.5%,[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-Cardenosa2004-318) respectively. Women with [complete androgen insensitivity syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complete_androgen_insensitivity_syndrome "Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome") (46,XY karyotype) never develop male sex characteristics and have normal and complete female [morphology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_\(biology\) "Morphology \(biology\)"), including breast development,[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-IIIBarbieri2013-319) yet have not been reported to develop breast cancer.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-pmid23044881-320) The risk of breast cancer in women with [Turner syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turner_syndrome "Turner syndrome") (45,XO karyotype) also appears to be significantly decreased, though this could be related to [ovarian failure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_failure "Ovarian failure") and [hypogonadism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypogonadism "Hypogonadism") rather than to genetics.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminizing_hormone_therapy#cite_note-pmid18282803-321)

Originating from an _ad hoc_ gathering of [finance ministers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finance_minister "Finance minister") in 1973, the G7 has since become a formal, high-profile venue for discussing and coordinating solutions to major [global issues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_global_issues "List of global issues"), especially in the areas of [trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade "Trade"), [security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security "Security"), [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy "Economy"), and [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change"). Each member's [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") or [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state"), along with the EU's [Commission president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Commission "President of the European Commission") and [European Council president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_European_Council "President of the European Council"), meet annually at the G7 Summit; other high-ranking officials of the G7 and the EU meet throughout the year. Representatives of other states and international organizations are often invited as guests, with [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") having been a formal member (as part of the [G8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G8 "G8")) from 1997 until its expulsion in 2014.
The G7 is not based on a treaty and has no permanent secretariat or office. It is organized through a presidency that rotates annually among the member states, with the presiding state setting the group's priorities and hosting the summit; France presides for 2026. While lacking a legal or institutional basis, the G7 is widely considered to wield significant international influence; it has catalyzed or spearheaded several major global initiatives, including efforts to combat the [HIV/AIDS pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS_pandemic "HIV/AIDS pandemic"), provide financial aid to developing countries, and [address climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_mitigation "Climate change mitigation") through the 2015 [Paris Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Agreement "Paris Agreement"). The group has been criticized by observers for its allegedly outdated and limited membership, narrow global representation, and inefficacy.
The G7 countries have together a population of about 780 million people (or almost 10% of the [world population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population "World population")) and account for around half of worldwide nominal [net wealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_worth "Net worth") and as of 2026 about 44% of world nominal [GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product") and about 28% of world GDP by [purchasing power parity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purchasing_power_parity "Purchasing power parity").

Of the 20 Nobel Prize winners affiliated with UTokyo in some way, twelve have earned degrees from the institution, with prizes won in five of the six categories, except for economics. This is the largest number among all universities in Asia.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tokyo#cite_note-150) However, when including other affiliates such as non-alumnus faculty members, the total number is on par with [Kyoto University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyoto_University "Kyoto University").[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tokyo#cite_note-151) The remainder consists of: [Hideki Yukawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hideki_Yukawa "Hideki Yukawa") (Physics, 1949), who served as a professor from 1942 for a few years;[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tokyo#cite_note-:7-152)[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tokyo#cite_note-153) [Charles H. Townes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_H._Townes "Charles H. RFC 6716[](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6716)                 Interactive Audio Codec          September 2012


   The use of Q17 values for the cosine terms in an otherwise Q16
   expression implicitly scales them by a factor of 2.  The
   multiplications in this recurrence may require up to 48 bits of
   precision in the result to avoid overflow.  In practice, each row of
   the recurrence only depends on the previous row, so an implementation
   does not need to store all of them.

   silk_NLSF2A() uses the values from the last row of this recurrence to
   reconstruct a 32-bit version of the LPC filter (without the leading
   1.0 coefficient), a32_Q17[k], 0 <= k < d2:

        a32_Q17[k]         = -(q_Q16[d2-1][k+1] - q_Q16[d2-1][k])
                             - (p_Q16[d2-1][k+1] + p_Q16[d2-1][k]))

        a32_Q17[d_LPC-k-1] =  (q_Q16[d2-1][k+1] - q_Q16[d2-1][k])
                             - (p_Q16[d2-1][k+1] + p_Q16[d2-1][k]))

   The sum and difference of two terms from each of the p_Q16 and q_Q16
   coefficient lists reflect the (1 + z**-1) and (1 - z**-1) factors of
   P and Q, respectively.  The promotion of the expression from Q16 to
   Q17 implicitly scales the result by 1/2.


###### 
4.2.7.5.7[](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6716#section-4.2.7.5.7).  Limiting the Range of the LPC Coefficients


   The a32_Q17[] coefficients are too large to fit in a 16-bit value,
   which significantly increases the cost of applying this filter in
   fixed-point decoders.  Reducing them to Q12 precision doesn't incur
   any significant quality loss, but still does not guarantee they will
   fit. silk_NLSF2A() applies up to 10 rounds of bandwidth expansion to
   limit the dynamic range of these coefficients.  Even floating-point
   decoders SHOULD perform these steps, to avoid mismatch.

   For each round, the process first finds the index k such that
   abs(a32_Q17[k]) is largest, breaking ties by choosing the lowest
   value of k.  Then, it computes the corresponding Q12 precision value,
   maxabs_Q12, subject to an upper bound to avoid overflow in subsequent
   computations:

              maxabs_Q12 = min((maxabs_Q17 + 16) >> 5, 163838)

   If this is larger than 32767, the procedure derives the chirp factor,
   sc_Q16[0], to use in the bandwidth expansion as

                                   (maxabs_Q12 - 32767) << 14
               sc_Q16[0] = 65470 - --------------------------
                                   (maxabs_Q12 * (k+1)) >> 2
